practicalSkillsWorkflowAgreement: Use choreograph to cast the scene and write a cause/effect timeline before implementation: antenna/gaze lead notice; head/glasses support inspection; the small hand supports invitation; text, stage and chrome remain static. Record the ending hold and interruption state in the same brief.

Use controlled auditions: preserve the baseline and shared opening, change one expressive decision at a time, and compare actual rendered sizes in both themes. More gestures or fewer gestures must each earn their place through a readable change in meaning.

Make responsive composition a storyboard deliverable. Review both the complete phone scene's eyeline/gesture relationship and the first viewport's reading order, rather than accepting no-overflow checks as complete staging approval.

Apply review-animations to purposeful controls and usable interruption while separating character content from interface feedback. Preserve explicit brief UI timings, native keyboard access to Play and informative reduced-motion stills.
Use animation-vocabulary to make requests precise. Label anticipation, follow-through and interruption accurately; do not use vocabulary or timing tables as substitutes for observation.

Keep forensic and perceptual evidence in separate fields for future engineers: normal-speed viewing asks whether the sequence reads; decoded frames and source locate the failure; device and human studies answer different questions. Record actual skill intake instead of treating catalog discovery as full reading.
